items.q: The typical HUS timeline runs: abdominal pain, then 2 days later bloody dysentery (evaluate & start antibiotics), and after 5 more days:
items.exp: Abdominal pain → 2 days → bloody dysentery → 5 days → 90-95% resolution; 5-10% HUS. (Book p755)

items.q: After the dysentery phase, the proportion that goes on to HUS is:
The treatment written for typical HUS is:
items.exp: Typical HUS treatment: conservative (evaluate & start antibiotics for the dysentery). (Book p755)

items.q: Atypical HUS presents with thrombocytopenia plus features of:
items.exp: Atypical HUS: features of 2° HTN (renal/endocrine); thrombocytopenia. (Book p755)

items.q: The mainstay of atypical HUS treatment, to be started within 24 hours, is:
items.exp: PLEX (plasma exchange therapy): within 24 hr; mainstay of treatment. (Book p755)

items.q: In atypical HUS, the costly terminal-complement drug and the immunosuppressant indication written for complement factor H mutation are:
items.exp: Eculizumab: costly; immunosuppressant in complement factor H mutation; renal transplant listed. (Book p755)

items.q: Recurrence of HUS after renal transplant is managed with:
items.exp: Recurrence post transplant: rituximab; eculizumab. (Book p755)

items.q: Match each feature with its column in the pre-renal vs ATN note — 1) Urine output in pre-renal injury 2) BUN/creatinine in ATN 3) Tubular injury in pre-renal injury … A) < 10:1 B) Normal C) Absent (−)
items.exp: Pre-renal: normal urine output, − edema, − tubular injury; ATN: decreased output, <10:1 BUN/Cr, + tubular injury. (Book p755)

items.q: The two BUN ratios written side by side in the note table are:
opts: > 20:1 in pre-renal injury vs < 10:1 in ATN
> 10:1 in pre-renal injury vs < 5:1 in ATN
> 30:1 in pre-renal injury vs < 20:1 in ATN

items.q: Which statement from the pre-renal vs ATN table is TRUE?
opts: Fluids are given in pre-renal injury but withheld in ATN, where edema and tubular injury are positive
Fluids are withheld in pre-renal injury and given in ATN
Edema is positive in pre-renal injury
Urine output is decreased in pre-renal injury
items.exp: Pre-renal: fluids given, edema −, tubular injury −; ATN: fluids withhold, edema +, tubular injury +. (Book p755)
